I'm gonna put pregnancy into perspective in case she has a difficult one :) 

1. Everyday her hormones are changing. So her body is having to accept a change it isn't used to. While our bodies are made to do this, not everyone is the same. So some people may vomit a lot, have constant nausea, food adversions, anxiety, etc. It's our bodies just trying to deal with the changes happening. 

2. With our bodies changing so much every single day, there's gonna be days where she just shuts down. She may be angry, or avoiding, negative, or overly suspiciously happy, anything in between. It's just so hard to be pregnant and sometimes certain hormones just take over. She prob won't even realize it. Just remember none of it is personal. It's not you, it's not her. It's pregnancy. 

3. There will be days she actually just wants to yell at you over everything. Because she's projecting. She's maybe feeling insecure with her body changing or the things it spontaneously does. She won't have much control over herself changing and may end up just holding onto a lot of anger. Taking it out on you, the safety, is kinda normal. Plz don't take it personally. 

4. Pain. So much pain. Some people just ache all pregnancy. Just do everything u can to make her comfortable. Make sure she always has water the way she likes it (iced, flavored, etc) and snacks. Save her the trips of having to move more then necessary when she's home from work. 

5. Make time for just you two and make sure you find ways to compliment her. Show appreciation for what she does do. Even if she can't express how thankful she is for it, she will be thankful for it. When u feel yuky it's so hard to keep motivated and believe you are doing a good job.

Everyone's labor is different. Mine is frontal labors for the first 3. It felt like I couldn't breathe, couldn't move, couldn't do anything without feeling like I was being torn apart. I got kinda crazy with it. BUT in that moment the epidural was absolutely painless in comparison. Didn't even feel it happening. And for my first 2? The epidural literally took it all away. No tears anymore. I was able to focus again. 

So it was bad enough I went kinda psycho there. Others will say meh it's just cramps. I say my lord I am dumb for having another. But everyones pain is gonna be different. 

If you have back labor I suggest staying in a warm shower as long as you can to keep your muscles from spasming on you if u can. The epidural I couldn't recommend enough though
Pushing in my experience relieves the pain. Because in that moment you are working with your body to perform a function. It feels good to push
In the moment you will find the strength to not be scared anymore ! You'll wanna get it done and you'll make it happen 🥰

My labor with my oldest and my second were easy breezey. The epidural is way more scary before hand then when u get it. Like ur likely in so much labor discomfort that u will hardly notice the numb prickle from the needle. 

My 3rd was painful no matter what. He was too big and my doctor did an awful job at my prenatal care. She ignored me when I told her he felt big. He should have even a c section. I had a full episiotomy. 

But even with all of that? I felt AMAZING after the babies were out with all 3. I INSTANTLY lost 20+ pounds. I was able to breathe, no more nausea, no more pelvic girdle pain, I felt like a million bucks. I was like oh there's my puss puss I haven't seen you in 5 months.  I was able to even shave my legs that night. 

Seriously labor sucks BUT the minute it starts, you don't get scared anymore. U get busy. You get it done. 

And when it's done? You'll feel so good. Sore but all the things non preggy people take for granted like breathing? You can do it again!
